name: 1620 Prairie Avenue — Robert Law house restored for 1904

documented_range.note: The 1904 target and no more, the draft's claim kept: Robinson 1886 draws the house and the T-1840 census carries it to 1904 on the 1904 Blue Book's listing at 1620. The 1911 sheet shows the frontage open, so the house was gone by then; when it was built and when it went are not read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the plate's L at its south wall (lot frame u 32.750, v -4.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line): 3.75 m south of the draft's origin, because the K01 rectangle runs across the whole front, the main body and its shallower south part together (see footprint). Placed through the T-1250 fit of Robinson 1886 plate 10, 4.54 m RMS, the weakest of the four T-1250 fits, plus about a pixel (0.35 m) of reading; rotation -0.579 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, the draft's.
placement.symbolic_location: 1620 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1620 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: One rectangle round the plate's L (trace r1886-1620-f, read by the draft as a 16.75 x 7.5 m main body and a 10.75 x 3.75 m shallower south part along the front): 16.75 m from the rear wall to the front by 11.25 m across the front. K01 builds one rectangle, so it CLOSES the 6.0 x 3.75 m notch the plate leaves at the south-west (rear) corner, 22.5 m2 over the traced 168 m2, as 1612's rectangle closes its court; a traced rear notch is K01's to learn (T-2347).

stories.note: RECONSTRUCTED: Robinson's 1886 atlas prints no storey count and the 1911 sheet, which would, no longer draws the house. Two storeys over a raised basement is the register's 'irregular earlier brick envelope' under a 'bounded roof' read at the height of its brick neighbours 1608 and 1612 (two storeys each on sheet 20); the 1898 Tribune drawing the register names would settle it and has not been read.

construction.note: Robinson 1886 plate 10 colours the building pink, the plate's brick (its frame buildings are yellow); the register's 'irregular earlier brick envelope' agrees. Built as a plain brick street front on common-brick side and rear walls (T-2341's K01 brick front); no stone front is read.

principal_floor_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the register's 'stoop' read as the high stoop of its brick neighbours: a principal floor 1.4 m above grade, inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES' range, the draft's own figure kept.

storey_heights_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: 3.9 m and 3.6 m, 1608's, inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES' ranges; the draft's 3.5 m upper storey left no room for the brick arch under the K10 cornice's bed moulding. Nothing read states them.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K03 common brick panel 1608 wears; the plate's pink says brick and nothing says which.

street_front_trim.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the register's 'arched windows' (its 1898 numbered drawing 'supports bay/arches'; the drawing is not read here) built as two rowlock rings on a segmental arch over every street window, the head this house's own side and rear walls already wear (T-2291), taught to the brick street front by T-1861 (`brick_heads`). The K01 wall cuts a rectangular hole, so the sash under each arch stays flat-headed and the arch springs from its jambs; an arched sash is a different hole and is not built. by_storey names K01's flat lintel only because brick_heads replaces it.

wall_head.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a K10 bracketed timber cornice round all four walls, the earlier Italianate brick house's usual eave; the register states only a 'bounded roof'.

roof_form.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the register's 'bounded roof' read as a low hip, the only roof K01 builds; the draft's hip kept.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a 30-degree hip, 1608's, inside the contract's ordinary range.

entrance_bay.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the door on the south bay of the front, where the plate's L carries its shallower south part; the bay takes the north half, as the draft had it.

front_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: three bays across the 11.25 m front: the door at 1.9 m from the south corner, a window at 5.4 m and the bay at 8.6 m, its eaves clear of the K10 corner bracket. The plate draws no openings.

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: four windows a storey along the 16.75 m south wall, rear to front; nothing draws them.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: three windows a storey across the rear wall; the register: 'rear windows remain reconstructed'.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: three windows a storey on the north wall, front to rear. It faces 1616 across a 4.7 m side yard (the lot runs to v 15.95 in this frame), not a party wall, so it is not left blank; nothing draws them.

sash_by_storey.note: RECONSTRUCTED: 1608's two-over-two sash, 1.0 m wide, 2.3 m in the principal storey and 1.9 m above, each under its brick arch.

roof_covering.note: RECONSTRUCTED: painted standing-seam tin with copper flashing and ridge roll, the K04 covering 1608 and 1600 wear.

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two brick stacks on the ridge line, one over each half of the house, 1608's stack and cap; nothing read places them.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K04 half-round copper gutters and round pipes to splash stones, as 1608's: one at the front's south corner, one midway along the south wall and one at each end of the rear; none on the north wall.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K06 two-over-two flat sash and area lights 1608 wears.

entrance_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K07 four-panel door under a two-light transom at the head of a straight stone stoop solved from the principal floor. front_yard_m is the street grid's own distance: the front stands 5.93 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line (the draft's street_u 22.679 less the 16.75 m body) and the walk begins 1 ft further out, 6.24 m.

boundary.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the register's 'lattice/iron boundary' built from the K11 ironwork kit as its scroll-band fence (a band of C-scrolls under the top rail, the kit's nearest to a lattice) on a stone curb along the street line, 5.93 m in front of the front face (the draft's street_u 22.679 less the 16.75 m body), from the north lot line to the gate of the carriage passage on the south; a pair of walk-gate leaves between stone piers on the walk to the stoop; a single walk gate 1.06 m clear across the south side yard's mouth beside the lot line (the yard is 7.7 m wide here, so the gate does not reach the house's south wall as 1808's does); and the kit's brick wall with piers, 1.2 m high, on the south lot line from the street back to u 12.0. The lot lines (s -7.711 and 15.951 along the front from the south corner) are the draft's lot_v for parcel prairie_1620 in this frame. The register names the boundary's kind and nothing else; its pattern, heights, gates and wall are the kit's.

bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the register's 'projecting bay' (its 1898 numbered drawing 'supports bay/arches', not read here) as the K08 canted bay 1608 wears, two storeys under a low tin hip on the north half of the front, centred 8.6 m from the south corner so its eaves clear the K10 corner bracket. Robinson's plate draws no bay at this scale, so neither its place nor its plan is read.

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws no front building at 1620. The T-1840 census (frontage-20-006, backcast_1886) stands the Robert Law house for 1904 because Robinson 1886 plate 10 prints 1620 against a brick house on lots 13-14 and the 1904 Blue Book lists the F. VanS. Hibbard household at the address (named record pa-1620-1904-correction); residence is inferred from that listing.

citations.citation: Robinson, E. Robinson's Atlas of the City of Chicago. New York: E. Robinson, 1886. Plate 10, "Part of 2.39.14 Assessors Div."
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from above 16th Street to 18th, as of 1886 -- a bound, from before, on the 1904 edge
Lot and subdivision lines, and the outlines of the houses at 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie that Glessner House names as standing in 1904 and gone by 1911
what_it_does_not_supply: Street widths: its bands are not drawn to the widths it prints (Prairie printed 66, drawn about 55 ft)
Anything as of 1904 on its own authority

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2334) in place by T-1861, under the draft's own id, as a K01 brick frontage: the plate's L under one rectangle, a canted bay on the north half of the front, segmental brick arches over the street windows, a high stoop, a bracketed cornice and a tin hip. Plan, place and brick are read off Robinson 1886 plate 10 (r1886-1620-f, through its T-1250 fit); the brief is the T-1837 register row frontage-20-006, which is not a source record; every height, opening, the roof and the trim are the kits' reconstruction (liberty L-k01-1620-law-1861). The rear stable is a separate record, still the draft's. The 1898 Tribune drawing the register names has not been read.
